title: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills
authors: Jianlyu Chen, Yuyang Hu, Hongjin Qian, Jiawei Liu, Wenqing Wei, Xiaolong Chen, Defu Lian, Zhicheng Dou, Chaozhuo Li, Qiwei Ye, Zheng Liu
lab: Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI), University of Science and Technology of China, Renmin University of China, Hong Kong Polytechnic University (corresponding authors Defu Lian, Zhicheng Dou, Zheng Liu)
date: September 2026 (arXiv v1, 2 September 2026; the only version so far)

code.title: VectorSpaceLab/AREX-Skill
code.note: Apache-2.0. The library (1,000 repository graphs, 5,353 SKILL.md files, 237 MB), its router and indexes, the DisCo CLI (built on the pi agent toolkit), the PaperBench, FrontierCS and PassNet skills, and two exported sessions (a Creator run on huggingface_hub and a Researcher run benchmarking vLLM against SGLang). The 75 MLE-bench skill graphs are not in it. This page reads it at commit ac3fe1a (3 September 2026). About 30 minutes for the README, the router and one repository graph

run_label: follow the router through the library
takeaway: Names the thing agent skills usually lack, operational knowledge (the practical know-how of getting a published method to actually run, which lives in READMEs and issues rather than papers), and distils it out of repositories into reusable skills both task-agnostically and task-oriented; the AREX-Skill Library is 5,000+ verified skills from 1,000 ML repos across 20 areas and 178 capability families, and on a GPT-5.5 backbone at fixed compute it buys +134.3% on MLE-bench, +34.4% PaperBench, +9.2% FrontierCS, +14.0% PassNet.
takeaway_note: The Takeaway above is the database property, quoted. Two corrections: none of the four benchmark gains uses the 1,000-repository library (each benchmark got its own task-specific or paper-derived skills), and the budget held fixed is the run-time budget only; building the MLE-bench skills took up to 24 more GPU-hours per competition.
verdict: Believe that the released library is real and counts out exactly (5,353 skills, 2,209 routes, the FrontierCS graph's 42 links), and that task-specific skills helped Codex on all four benchmarks. Do not read the headline numbers as the library's effect or as free: none of the four results uses the 1,000-repository library, the MLE-bench skills came from up to 24 GPU-hours of exploration on each competition that the "fixed budget" leaves out, the FrontierCS skill runs used 1.8 times the tokens, and only MLE-bench reports repeated runs.

resources.t: AREX-Skill README and the repository-skills router
resources.n: The router's SKILL.md is 48 lines: the routing procedure and the 20-area map. Then open one area page, one family page and one repository graph (vllm is a good one) to see what an agent actually reads.

resources.t: The released Researcher session: vLLM against SGLang
resources.n: A five-hour session exported as one HTML file (download it and open locally), plus the benchmark report. The Run tab of this page replays its skill reads.
The one graph behind the FrontierCS result: a recovery router and eight modules. Its README explains when it activates and the champion, challenger and fallback roles.

resources.t: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
resources.n: The SKILL.md format and progressive disclosure that this paper builds on.
The 75 Kaggle competitions and the Any Medal metric; read the setup section for the standard 24-hour budget per competition.
The 20 ICML 2024 papers, the rubric-based replication score and its LLM judge.
Open-ended problems with measurable but unknown optima; the Agent Track and its public leaderboard.

resources.t: From anatomy to smells: an empirical study of SKILL.md in agent skills
resources.n: The paper's evidence that hand-written skills are inconsistent at scale, the problem automatic distillation is meant to fix.

kb.t: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work - Until They Don't
kb.n: The mechanistic account: skills act as procedural anchors, and they add a failure mode of their own (guidance misapplied or ignored, 10.0% of the skill arm's labels). The caution this paper only half engages with.

kb.t: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
kb.n: Skills are one component a self-built harness has to assemble; this paper is the supply side of that component, at library scale.

kb.t: Terminal-Universe: Turning Agent Trajectories into Scalable Terminal Environments
kb.n: Same week, same shape of idea applied to environments: mine artifacts that already exist (trajectories) for something the field was making by hand.

kb.t: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
kb.n: Listed with Prime Agent on the old page as a different answer to the same complaint about hand-made agent context.

kb.t: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
kb.n: Lets the agent version its own skills inline and finds the policy underuses it; Repo-To-Skill removes the authoring burden instead.
